questions.statement: Which possessive adjective is used for "She"?
questions.context: Identifying a possessive adjective for a female subject.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "His" is for "He".
Correct! "Her" is the possessive adjective for "She".
Incorrect. "Its" is for "It".
Incorrect. "Your" is for "You".

questions.explanation:
The student identifies the basic mapping between subject pronouns and possessive adjectives.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the correct way to say that the book belongs to Juan using the Saxon Genitive?
questions.context: Expressing that a book belongs to Juan.

options.feedback: Incorrect. This lacks the possessive 's.
Incorrect. This sounds like "Juan is a book".
Correct! The 's indicates that the book belongs to Juan.
Incorrect. While grammatically possible, "Juan's book" is the standard and more natural way to express possession in English.

questions.explanation:
The student remembers the basic rule for the Saxon Genitive to express possession.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: "We are students. ________ school is in Bogotá."

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Our" is the possessive adjective; it doesn't need an apostrophe.
Correct! "Our" is the possessive adjective for "We".
Incorrect. "Your" is for "You".
Incorrect. "Their" is for "They".

questions.explanation:
The student understands the use of the possessive adjective for the first person plural.

questions.subject: ingles

options.feedback: Incorrect. "It's" means "It is".
Correct! "Its" is the possessive adjective for animals or things.
Incorrect. "His" is for male humans (though sometimes used for pets, "its" is the general rule).
Incorrect. "Her" is for female humans.

questions.explanation:
The student distinguishes between the contraction "it's" and the possessive adjective "its".

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: "I have a car. ________ color is blue."
questions.context: Describing the color of someone's car.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "My" would refer to me, not the car's color.
Correct! We use "Its" to refer to the color of the car (an object).
Incorrect. "It's" is "It is".
Incorrect. "His" is for a male person.

questions.explanation:
The student applies the possessive adjective "its" to refer to a characteristic of an inanimate object.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Based on the text, who is Elena?
questions.context:
A description of a family tree.
"Carlos is Maria's husband. Elena is Carlos and Maria's daughter."

options.feedback: Incorrect. She is her daughter.
Correct! The text says she is the daughter of Carlos and Maria.
Incorrect. She is his daughter.
Incorrect. Not mentioned and illogical.

questions.explanation:
The student applies knowledge of the Saxon Genitive to understand family relationships in a text.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: "The ________ toys are in the box." (The toys belong to the boys)

options.feedback: Incorrect. This means only one boy.
Correct! For plural nouns ending in -s, we just add an apostrophe.
Incorrect. Plural nouns ending in -s do not need another 's'.
Incorrect. Missing the possessive marker.

questions.explanation:
The student applies the specific rule for the Saxon Genitive with plural nouns ending in -s.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: Choosing the correct combination of possessives.

options.text: This is my brother's room. Its is very big.
options.feedback: Incorrect. "Its" is a possessive adjective; "It" (subject) is needed here.

options.text: This is my brother's room. It is very big.
options.feedback: Correct! "Brother's" shows possession and "It" refers to the room.

options.text: This is my brothers room. It is very big.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Missing the apostrophe for possession.

options.text: This is mine brother room. It is very big.
options.feedback: Incorrect. "Mine" is a possessive pronoun, and "brother" needs the genitive 's.

questions.explanation:
The student analyzes the difference between possessive markers and subject pronouns in a context.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.context:
A complex family description.
"My father's name is Jorge. Jorge's sister is my Aunt Clara. Clara's car is red."

options.feedback: Incorrect. Jorge is the father, Clara is the one with the red car.
Incorrect. My father is Jorge.
Correct! Clara is the aunt, and the text says "Clara's car is red".
Incorrect. The car belongs to Clara.

questions.explanation:
The student analyzes a sequence of possessive relationships to identify the owner of an object.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Why is the apostrophe after the 's' in "customers'"?
questions.context:
Evaluating the use of possessives in a formal context.
"Welcome to our company. We value our customers' feedback to improve our services."

options.text: Because there is only one customer.
options.feedback: Incorrect. That would be "customer's".

options.text: Because it refers to the feedback of many customers.
options.feedback: Correct! The plural "customers" adds just an apostrophe for possession.
Incorrect. The apostrophe location depends on the owner, not the object.
Incorrect. It is a correct and standard grammatical rule.

questions.explanation: The student evaluates and explains the grammatical logic behind a specific punctuation mark in a possessive context.
